Connect for Digital and Financial Inclusion: Pilot, Moroto District, Uganda

	Connect for Digital and Financial Inclusion: Pilot, Moroto District, Uganda
	Period of Performance
	2026-11-02 to 2027-04-30
	1. Background
[Partner Name] (henceforth, referred to as "partner") is the implementing partner for the work described in this Work Order.


Many adults in Karamoja do not have their own phone, a SIM card registered in their own name, a national identity (ID) card or an active mobile money wallet. About 20% of residents own a phone, and partners estimate that about 35% of adults hold a national ID card. Without these four items an adult cannot use digital financial services or save and send money safely in their own name. Dimagi is running a pilot, Connect for Digital and Financial Inclusion, to help every adult in a small area hold all four. An adult who holds an accepted ID, a SIM and mobile money wallet in their own name and a working phone, has completed a short training session and has received a small deposit into their wallet, is complete.


The pilot runs on Connect, Dimagi's platform for contracting Locally-Led organizations (LLOs) and paying them for verified work. Frontline Workers (FLWs) learn the workflow on their phones and record every step in the Connect app; Dimagi verifies each record and pays the partner for each verified result. The pilot also compares two ways of delivering the same package, community events and door-to-door visits, to learn which reaches more adults, faster and at lower cost.
2. Scope of Work
This Work Order covers field delivery for the pilot: finding and enrolling every resident adult in the agreed villages, then following each adult over repeated contacts until they hold all four items or the field period ends. The partner tracks each adult individually, from a first household visit or community event through ID support, SIM and wallet registration by a licensed agent, phone handover where needed, and a training session, to a verified completion. The timeline in section 5 lists eight periods of unequal length, not calendar weeks.


For each engagement, the partner will:


* Build a household list for each village from the village register held by the Local Council 1 (LC1) chairperson, checked with Village Health Teams (VHTs) and mapped with GPS
* Register every household, screen each listed person for age and residency, and enrol every resident adult aged 18 or over in the Connect app, with consent, whatever items they already hold
* Record, for each adult, which of the four items they hold, seeing the ID card and the handset rather than relying on what is said
* Support adults without an accepted ID to apply to the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA) and to collect their printed cards, and follow up until the card is in hand
* Arrange for licensed MTN or Airtel agents to register each adult's SIM and wallet in their own name, with the adult present, at activation events or at home where agents may register there
* Buy, store and hand over one basic feature phone to each adult who has no working phone of their own and whose ID card is recorded, noting the handset serial number and taking a photo at handover
* Deliver a 15 to 30 minute hands-on session to every enrolled adult on PIN safety, fees, sending and receiving money, checking the balance, saving and avoiding scams
* Follow up each adult, by home visit, community event, agent visit or phone call, until they complete or the field period ends, and record every contact, including any refusal, in the Connect app
* Run community events in the villages Dimagi assigns to the events approach, and door-to-door visits in the others
* Field a separate team, not the delivery FLWs, for the household baseline survey before any part of the pilot is announced
* Keep a phone stock register and reconcile it weekly against verified handovers


The partner will not:


* Register, hold, carry or hand out SIM cards for anyone, or ask for or record any PIN
* Give a phone to an adult who already owns a working phone, or more than one phone to any adult
* Send deposits or village bonuses, which Dimagi sends
* Promise or suggest any future payment, benefit or programme to participants or communities
* Collect fingerprints or other biometric data
* Enrol people under 18 or people who do not live in the agreed villages
* Deploy FLWs before 06:00 or after 19:00
* Recover the cost of a phone from any participant
3. Geographic Coverage
The pilot covers 3 to 5 villages (LC1) in about half of one parish, Loputuk or Nadunget, in Moroto District, Karamoja, Uganda: about 1,650 resident adults. The partner will confirm the chosen villages and their adult populations with Dimagi during November scoping, before field work starts. Dimagi assigns each village to the community events approach or the door-to-door approach by lot before the baseline survey.
4. Deliverables and Verification
4.1 Primary Deliverable
The primary deliverable is a verified Connect record for every resident adult in the agreed villages, showing their starting point, each step completed and its date, and whether they are complete. Dimagi suggests aiming for at least 90% of resident adults enrolled (about 1,480) and at least 55% of enrolled adults complete by 28 February 2027. Though these are not hard requirements, they are the targets the pilot is judged against. The partner hands over adults still in progress at the end of field work with their status recorded.
4.2 Definition of a Verified Unit
A unit qualifies as "verified" and is payable under this Work Order only when all of the following are met:


* Adult enrolled: a resident adult aged 18 or over has consented, their residency is confirmed against the village register or by village leaders, the record carries a photo, GPS and the status of each of the four items, and no earlier enrolment exists for that adult under the same national ID number, phone number, handset serial number, or name, birth year and village
* ID obtained: for an adult who had no accepted ID when enrolled, the FLW has seen and photographed the physical national ID card and recorded its number, and no earlier ID result exists for that adult
* Adult completed: on the same day the FLW has seen the ID card and a working handset of the adult's own, the adult has shown on their handset (by dialling *197#) that the SIM is registered to their own ID number, the wallet is active and its registered name matches the ID and the enrolment record, all seven training topics are recorded, and no earlier completion exists for that adult
* The FLW assigned to that adult submits every unit between 06:00 and 19:00, and the unit passes Connect's automatic checks


Dimagi verifies units through Connect's automatic checks on every submission; a daily review of all records for duplicate national ID numbers, phone numbers, handset serial numbers, and matching name, birth year and village; a review of photos, with a sample checked by a person; and calls to a random sample of completed adults by a team outside the partner's organization. Units that fail one or more criteria are not payable. Where the daily review flags a possible duplicate, Dimagi holds payment for the flagged unit until it is resolved.
4.3 Reporting Deliverables
* Weekly progress report: adults enrolled, ID results and completions by village and approach, plus the phone stock register (received, in store, handed over, lost)
* Monthly performance review with Dimagi, covering coverage, contacts per adult, delays at NIRA or with agents, and any field risks
* Close-out report by 15 March 2027: coverage by village and approach, the list of adults still in progress with the item each is waiting on and how long they have waited, a final stock reconciliation and receipts for all costs paid at cost

6. Payment Terms
6.1 Total Not-to-Exceed
Dimagi's total financial commitment under this Work Order is UGX 185,400,000, not-to-exceed, inclusive of all field collection costs, FLW compensation, supervision, transport, and partner reporting time.
6.2 Payment Schedule
#
	Milestone
	% of Cap
	Amount (UGX)
	Trigger / Deliverable
	Expected Timing
	1
	Mobilization advance
	40%
	UGX 74,160,000
	Signature of this Work Order; funds scoping, the baseline survey, partner start-up and the first phone order
	Within 10 working days of signature
	2
	Monthly payments and final reconciliation
	60%
	UGX 111,240,000
	Monthly, against verified units and receipted costs; the final balance on acceptance of the close-out report
	Monthly from January 2027; final payment within 30 days of acceptance and no later than 30 April 2027
	

Dimagi will pay for verified units at the following per-milestone rates, for each verified milestone in each adult's sequence: UGX 11,000 per adult enrolled, UGX 11,000 per ID obtained (only for adults who started without an accepted ID) and UGX 23,000 per adult completed, each covering FLW pay, supervision, transport and reporting. Each adult earns each milestone at most once. Where the partner's solicitation response proposes different rates and Dimagi accepts them in writing before signature, those rates replace these. No more than 30 verified units of each type per FLW per day are payable, and no more than 150 enrolments, 70 ID results and 100 completions per FLW over the Work Order; Dimagi pays verified units within a ceiling of UGX 57,000,000. Dimagi reimburses the following at cost against receipts, each within its own ceiling: phones, UGX 57,250,000 at no more than UGX 50,000 per phone delivered; the baseline survey and scoping, UGX 26,625,000; partner start-up, UGX 17,750,000; the NIRA ID drive, UGX 17,750,000; and community event days, UGX 9,000,000. The mobilization advance is recoverable: verified units and receipted costs accrue against it until it is fully drawn down, after which Dimagi pays them monthly. At close-out the partner will hand any phones bought but not handed over to Dimagi or its nominee, reconciled against the stock register; Dimagi does not reimburse phones that are neither handed over against a verified record, held in stock, nor reported lost within 24 hours with a written explanation, and the partner bears the cost of those. If this Work Order ends early, or field work has not started by 15 December 2026, the partner will return any part of the advance not yet covered by verified units or receipted costs within 30 days. Dimagi accepts or returns the close-out report within 10 working days of receiving it, against the reporting requirements in section 4.3; if Dimagi does not respond within that time, the report is deemed accepted.

	8. Permissions, Ethics, and Compliance
8.1 Permissions
The partner is responsible for securing all in-country permissions required to conduct the field activities, including:


* Approval from the NIRA district officer for ID enrolment and card-collection activities
* Notification of the Resident District Commissioner (RDC) and the District Community Development Officer (DCDO)
* Entry through the LC1 chairperson of each village
* Agreement with MTN and Airtel licensed agents or dealers to register SIMs and wallets at events or at home
* Any security clearance required for field work in Moroto District


The partner will provide Dimagi with copies of all written permissions or notifications obtained.
8.2 Ethics
The work collects personal information about adults (names, birth years, national ID numbers, phone numbers and photos) but no health or clinical data. The partner will take informed consent from every adult before enrolment, and a separate, optional consent before recording whether an adult agrees to be contacted later by other services. The partner will explain clearly that the pilot does not promise any future money. Dimagi completes a data protection assessment for Uganda before field work starts, and the partner will follow its requirements.
8.3 Security and Duty of Care
The partner retains sole responsibility for the safety and security of its field teams. The partner will not deploy FLWs to areas where the prevailing security situation, in the partner's professional judgement, poses an unacceptable risk.
9. Data Handling
Field
	Value
	Project overview
	Connect for Digital and Financial Inclusion pilot: enrolling every resident adult in the agreed villages of Moroto District and following each one until they hold an accepted ID, a SIM and wallet in their own name and a working phone
	Data subjects
	Resident adults aged 18 and over in the agreed villages, and the households they live in
	Personal information processed
	Name, sex, birth year, village, GPS location, photos of the adult, their ID card, handset and wallet name screen, national ID number, phone number, handset serial number, SIM and wallet status, consent responses
	Purpose of processing
	To deliver and verify the pilot, prevent duplicate enrolment and distributions, and measure coverage, time and cost
	Technical and organizational security
	Encrypted on the phone and in transit; role-based access in Connect; FLWs see only the adults assigned to them
	Measures by Partner
	No copies of records or photos outside the Connect app; no sharing with any third party; no PINs ever recorded; the partner reports a lost phone to Dimagi within 24 hours
	Data storage location
	Connect servers in the United States, subject to the Uganda data protection assessment
	Data protection
	Applicable Ugandan data protection law and Dimagi's data protection policies; records shared outside the pilot only under a separate written agreement and with the adult's consent
